thread:
jamie: Quick sync  we need to finalize the onboarding/workflow for customers who opt into cross-account peering for the control plane in private VPCs. Main goals: minimal blast radius, clear audit trail, and reversible revocation without messy routing leftovers. Two high-level runtimes: peering with a signed acceptance manifest vs keep-all-outbound-relay. Which is our default?

alex: I think a manifest + state machine is the most operable. Relay-only is safest from a network surface perspective but causes higher recurring costs and latency. Manifest lets us automate housekeeping (create route table entries, set prefix lists).

priya: From support/product: if we present peering as "opt-in with signed manifest" during onboarding, customers understand responsibility. Need copy that explains egress billing, CIDR validation, and revoke semantics.

sara: Security concerns: manifest must be signed by a customer-admin key (KMS-backed) and include an expiration. Post-peering we should run a verification job: check there are no additional routes from customer's VPC into our control-plane subnets, verify SG/NACLs are not overly permissive, and confirm no overlapping IPs exist. If anything is off, auto-revoke and pivot to relay.

mike: Revocation is key. On delete we must remove routes and NAT entries and invalidate any ephemeral tokens. Automate cleanup across clouds (AWS BGP aside). Also add a soft-grace period for customers to fix an issue before hard delete — e.g., PEER_DEGRADED -> notify -> 24h -> revoke.

jamie: Proposal: manifest fields: version, customer_id, allowed_prefixes, manifest_nonce, expires_at, acceptance_signature, provider_hints (cloud, region), billing_consent_flag. Store only signed manifest and verification hashes. Example snippet in onboarding UI: 
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "customer_id": "acct-12345",
  "allowed_prefixes": ["10.60.1.0/24"],
  "provider": "aws",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "expires_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
  "manifest_nonce": "b2f0...",
  "billing_consent": "true",
  "acceptance_signature": "<signed-by-customer>"
}
```

infra-bot: Note: AWS supports prefix-lists and managed route propagation filters; GCP requires more IAM checks and custom route handling. We'll need cloud-specific enforcement modules. Also ensure manifest rotation when control-plane prefix set changes.

sec-bot: checklist: (1) signature uses customer's KMS public key, (2) manifest expiry enforced, (3) audit log entry with manifest hash & timestamp, (4) automated revoke-on-policy-violation, (5) retention policy for signed blobs.

priya: UX: onboarding two-step: a) present the manifest + billing delta estimate b) customer signs via CLI or console (we accept signed blob) c) we create peering and run automated audit d) customer sees status REQUESTED -> PROVISIONED -> VERIFIED (or QUARANTINED). Provide "re-run verification" and "revoke peering" buttons.

alex: State machine sketch: REQUESTED -> PEER_CREATED -> VERIFICATION_PENDING -> VERIFIED -> ACTIVE. Failure transitions: VERIFICATION_FAILED -> PEER_QUARANTINED (notify customer + SRE) -> AUTO_FAILOVER_TO_RELAY -> AWAITING_CUSTOMER_FIX -> REVOKED (if not fixed). Each transition emits an audit event with manifest hash.

mike: Operational playbook: include commands for manual revoke, route cleanup, and for re-issuing a manifest after prefix changes. Also include a cost alert if relay fallback triggers a significant egress charge so finance can notify sales.

sara: For compliance we should record the acceptance event with a signed timestamp and manifest hash. That should be exportable as a PDF for customers with enterprise compliance needs. Keep retention configurable per account.

jamie: Canarying idea: enable peering to a canary control-plane AZ/subnet first for 12-24h, run verification and traffic tests (latency + correctness), then expand. We can represent canary as an extra manifest flag: "canary:true" and expansion requires a new signed acceptance for the larger prefix set.

infra-bot: Implementation notes: overlapping CIDR detection must return actionable errors (e.g., "overlap with existing customer CIDR x.x.x.x/yy"). Automate route cleanups in same transaction if cloud APIs allow. Add idempotent APIs for manifest submit so retries safe.

sec-bot: make sure the acceptance_signature TTL and manifest expiry are validated before any peering creation. Also encrypt manifests at rest using our HSM-backed envelope.

jamie: OK next steps: (1) engineer spike for cloud-specific enforcement modules + cleanup playbook (infra), (2) manifest schema PR and signing integration (jamie + sec), (3) onboarding UI mock + user copy (priya + alex), (4) playbook + billing guardrails (mike). I'll open RFC PR and link these tasks. Any objections?

priya: No objections. I'll draft the onboarding copy and include the checkbox language and a simple cost explainer.

alex: I'll prototype the state machine UI and the transition webhooks we need for audit events.

mike: I'll work the cost model and the support-runbook for PEER_DEGRADED scenarios. Also create alerting for when fallback relay increases our egress > threshold.

jamie: Great. Filing a follow-up issue INFRA-8001 for the manifest lifecycle spike. Closing thread; will track in the RFC PR. :rocket:
